subject: Renewal proposal: price hold + onboarding credit with staged capacity uplift
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@fjordline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: price hold + onboarding credit with staged capacity uplift

Hi Helen —

Thanks again for the honest conversation on Tuesday. Per our follow-up, attached is a clean first pass at a renewal structure that we think hits your two priorities: (1) preserve a price hold to avoid surprise per-token increases through Q3 while you finish the EU procurement cycle, and (2) give you explicit onboarding/offtake credits to offset cost during the migration of two internal services to Redwood.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Term: 12 months (Jul 1, 2025 — Jun 30, 2026)
- Price hold: current rate held for first 6 months (Jul–Dec 2025)
- Staged uplift: committed footprint increases by 25% at month 7 with a calibrated 30-day ramp window
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit equal to 2 months of committed spend applied in first invoice cycle
- True-up: quarterly true-up with 30-day notice for overages; overages billed at standard overage rate thereafter

Attached: Redwood_Termsheet_Proposed_v1.pdf (term highlights) and Fjordline_Onboarding_SOW.xlsx (ops runbook + milestones).

If this looks roughly aligned I can push a v2 that includes invoice timing and a short DocuSign-ready addendum for your procurement team. Would you like us to preserve the price hold through the end of Q3 (Sep 30) instead of Dec 31 if procurement signoff is delayed? That is one levers we can toggle.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Director, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Appreciate the price-hold idea; that helps buy us time while procurement completes the vendor review. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) Can you confirm whether the onboarding credit can be applied against July invoice or must it be credited after completion of onboarding milestones? Our finance team prefers credits applied up front as a negative invoice line so it hits our P&L in Q3.
2) For the staged uplift, what visibility will we have into usage thresholds triggering the increased commit? We need a 14-day heads-up before the commit re-allocates upward so our infra team can validate limits.
3) Do you have a short form PO (or DocuSign flow) we can use to start the procurement queue? Procurement will want to review Master Agreement redlines — can you highlight any non-standard terms?

I’m looping in procurement and Tom on this thread. If we can get a DocuSign-ready sheet and the invoice treatment clarified, I can push this into our next vendor meeting on Monday.

Thanks,
Helen Park
Director, Cloud Engineering — Fjordline Solutions

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Jun 2025 08:29:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: price hold + onboarding credit with staged capacity uplift

Jordan / Ben —

Quick internal note before we send v2 to procurement. I like the structure but recommend the following tweaks so procurement can approve faster and ops has clear guardrails: 

- Price hold window: change to a 90-day guaranteed hold from go-live (easier to explain than calendar months) — gives Fjordline a guaranteed window without calendar churn.
- Onboarding credit: front-load 50% at invoice 1, remainder after completion of milestone 2 (migration of service B). This addresses their P&L ask while protecting us from partial deliveries.
- Staged uplift: build a 14-day notice clause and a soft cap for month-over-month scaling (no more than +15% month-over-month without re-negotiation).
- Add a short SLA credit schedule if latency breaches happen during ramp (simple % credit per incident, capped). Procurement likes explicit remediation language.

I’ll sketch these into the terms and Ben can produce v2 with clear invoice lines and a DocuSign-ready signature block.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Helen / Tom / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick responses — attached is Redwood_Termsheet_Proposed_v2.pdf which incorporates Marissa’s suggested edits and clarifies invoice treatment. Key points in this v2: 

1) Price hold: guaranteed 90 days from mutual go-live (defined in SOW). If procurement signoff delays beyond 90 days, price hold automatically extends on a month-to-month basis while procurement review is active (with a maximum extension of 3 months total).

2) Onboarding credit: total credit equals two months of the committed monthly spend. 50% applied to first invoice as a negative line item, 50% applied after Milestone 2 sign-off (SOW tab).

3) Staged uplift / commit change: committed capacity increases by 25% at the scheduled uplift date. Redwood will provide a 14-day notice and a dashboard export to Fjordline showing projected monthly token burn. Any proposed >15% month-over-month increase requires joint ops review and explicit re-commit.

4) SLA remediation: simple credit schedule for latency >500ms on average during ramp window (credit tier table in v2).

5) Procurement redlines: we preserved standard MSA language; non-standard asks (data residency addendum, indemnity cap) are highlighted in the redline column.

Attachments: Redwood_Termsheet_Proposed_v2.pdf, Fjordline_Onboarding_SOW.xlsx
DocuSign (signature-ready): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/abc123
Internal link to deal: https://redwoodapp.example.com/deals/DL-2025-0789

If procurement is comfortable with the extension language and invoice mechanics, we can generate a short PO-friendly page and route to DocuSign for signatures. Jordan / Marissa — if you want me to soften extension language on the hold, say now.

Best,
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
